answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by anchoring identity to cryptographic attestation chains and zero-knowledge proofs. Operating like a secure jetty against a plume of malicious traffic, verified nodes validate credentials while a dynamic staking function imposes exponential capital exhaustion ($O(2^k)$ bonding costs) on any coordinated Sybil swarm, ensuring an attacker cannot cheaply mass-fabricate autonomous identities to mimic a human sonnet.
